forces.title: Government Policy Drives EV Adoption in Commercial Mobility
forces.description: Government initiatives such as the PM E-DRIVE Scheme (Rs 10,900 crore outlay) and the PM e-Bus Sewa Scheme (Rs 57,613 crore outlay for 10,000 electric buses) provide significant demand incentives and support for charging infrastructure. States like Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka also have ambitious targets for electrifying commercial and logistics fleets, and public transport buses. These policies accelerate EV adoption in the CV sector, strengthening supply-chain resilience and encouraging investment in EV components.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Shift Towards Electronics and Software-Enabled Components
forces.description: The CV industry is undergoing a structural transformation from mechanical to technology-intensive. EV adoption in CVs means components like batteries (40-50% of vehicle cost) and electronics (23% of BOM) become dominant, significantly higher than in ICE vehicles. This necessitates retooling and R&D for manufacturers, expanding the addressable market for advanced electronics, sensors, and embedded software in powertrain technologies. The industry is evolving towards a more technology and engineering-oriented ecosystem.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: AI-Driven Operational Efficiency and Predictive Maintenance for Fleets
forces.description: AI applications are set to revolutionize commercial mobility, enhancing asset productivity and profitability. For high-utilization segments like buses and fleet operations, AI-driven predictive maintenance, battery-health forecasting, intelligent charging management, and route optimization will minimize downtime and translate into significant revenue gains. This transforms repair centers into vehicle-health management providers and enables dealerships to anticipate customer needs, moving the industry towards data-centric mobility and away from product-centric models.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: Growing Domestic Demand and Aftermarket Opportunities
forces.description: Domestic OEM demand remains a primary growth driver for the auto ancillary industry, with healthy volume growth expected across commercial vehicles in FY27. The aftermarket segment is also a stable contributor, driven by an expanding vehicle parc (expected to reach 430-435 million units by 2030) and increasing average vehicle age. This provides resilient replacement demand and supports overall industry growth. Increased investment in road infrastructure also acts as a significant demand-side driver for commercial vehicles.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Dependence on Imported Critical EV Components Remains a Challenge
forces.description: Despite localisation efforts, the auto ancillary industry, which supplies components to CVs, remains dependent on imported critical components such as semiconductors, battery cells, sensors, and advanced electronics. While the PLI-ACC Scheme aims to establish domestic battery manufacturing, its progress is slow. This continued reliance on imports creates vulnerability to geopolitical developments, volatility in freight costs, and commodity prices, which can pressure profitability, particularly for export-oriented manufacturers, and hinders domestic value addition.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

forces.title: Favorable GST and Financing Options Boosting EV Sales
forces.description: The reduction of GST on electric vehicles from 12% to 5% and on chargers from 18% to 5% acts as a significant tailwind for the adoption of electric commercial vehicles. Additionally, new financing partnerships, such as Euler Motors with Annapurna Finance and VinFast India with CSB Bank, are expanding customized financing options for electric three- and four-wheelers. These initiatives improve accessibility and affordability for fleet operators, small businesses, and last-mile delivery entrepreneurs, accelerating EV penetration in the CV segment.

forces.title: Electrification Targets Reshaping CV Market Landscape
forces.description: India has set ambitious targets for EV penetration in the commercial vehicle segment, aiming for 70% in commercial vehicles and 40% in buses by 2030. NITI Aayog has even proposed pilot programs for 100% electrification of buses and freight vehicles. These strong governmental objectives fundamentally reshape demand, driving substantial investments in e-bus deployment and infrastructure, and compelling CV manufacturers to accelerate their EV portfolios. States like Tamil Nadu are also setting targets for electric bus fleets and battery manufacturing policies.

forces.title: MSME and Services Sector Credit Growth Boosting CV Demand
forces.description: Bank credit growth is broad-based, with MSMEs and the services sector identified as major growth drivers. MSME lending has increased significantly, and services-sector lending has strengthened due to higher borrowings by NBFCs and commercial real estate activities. Since MSMEs and the services sector are key end-users of commercial vehicles for logistics, last-mile delivery, and other business operations, their robust growth and access to formal credit directly translate into increased demand for CVs.

forces.title: Auto Ancillary Industry poised for Global Sourcing Opportunities
forces.description: The Indian auto component industry is strengthening its position as a global sourcing hub, supported by manufacturing competitiveness, engineering capabilities, and an expanding domestic market. Auto component exports are projected to reach US$ 70-100 billion by FY30. This includes components relevant for CVs. Supply-chain diversification efforts by global companies are increasingly shifting sourcing and manufacturing to India, creating significant opportunities for Indian auto component firms to integrate into global value chains and advanced component manufacturing.

forces.title: Focus on Multi-Pathway Mobility Solutions
forces.description: India's mobility transition is expected to remain multi-pathway, supporting not just EVs, but also hybrids, flex-fuel vehicles, ethanol-blended fuel platforms, and CNG vehicles. This creates diverse opportunities across fuel systems, emission-control technologies, sensors, electronic control units, and lightweight materials for commercial vehicle manufacturers and their component suppliers. This approach acknowledges varied operational needs and infrastructure availability, promoting a broader spectrum of powertrain solutions for the CV sector.
forces.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry Poised for Sustained Growth and Value Addition in FY27
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings projects the Indian auto ancillary industry to grow 8-9% in FY27, driven by strong OEM demand across segments like commercial vehicles, increasing component content per vehicle, and resilient replacement demand. The shift towards electronics-intensive and cleaner mobility platforms, including EVs, is expanding opportunities for high-value automotive systems. Localisation initiatives are crucial to reduce import dependence. The sector benefits from cost pass-through mechanisms with OEMs, providing earnings resilience. However, technological advancements and import reliance on critical components remain key monitorables.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Auto Ancillary Industry to Grow 8-9% in FY27

viewpoints.title: AI to Revolutionize Commercial Mobility with Predictive Maintenance and Efficiency Gains
viewpoints.description: KPMG believes AI will be as crucial as electrification in automotive retail, particularly for commercial mobility. For fleet operators and bus services, AI-driven predictive maintenance, battery-health forecasting, intelligent charging, and route optimization will dramatically improve asset productivity and profitability. The high utilization of two-wheelers, three-wheelers, buses, and fleet operations means every hour of downtime results in lost revenue, making AI an engine for operational efficiency and reliability. This transformation moves mobility from product-centric to data-centric.
viewpoints.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

viewpoints.title: India's EV Market, Including Commercial Vehicles, Set for Strong and Steady Growth
viewpoints.description: IBEF anticipates strong and steady growth for India's electric vehicle market through 2030, supported by robust government leadership and schemes like PM E-DRIVE. The government aims for 70% EV penetration in commercial vehicles and 40% in buses by 2030, indicating significant future adoption. While 2W and 3W currently dominate EV volumes, policies like the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme and state-level electrification targets for cargo vehicles highlight a clear push towards electric commercial mobility, driving expansion across all EV segments.

viewpoints.title: Indian Banking Sector Resilient in FY27, Supporting Vehicle Financing and MSME Growth
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings expects the Indian banking sector's resilience to continue in FY27, with credit growth outpacing deposits. This broad-based credit expansion, driven by retail lending, MSMEs, and NBFCs, is positive for Commercial Vehicles. Vehicle financing, in particular, benefits from strong automobile and electric vehicle sales. MSMEs and the services sector, both major growth drivers for bank credit, are key consumers of commercial vehicles, implying sustained demand for CVs and their financing.
